# ast-pack — complete documentation (single file for LLMs and AI agents)

> Source: https://github.com/ginckl/ast-pack · generated by scripts/build_llms_full.py from README.md, AGENT_GUIDE.md, benchmarks/RESULTS.md, schema.json and module docstrings.

---

# ast-pack

> **TL;DR — ast-pack builds the smallest correct LLM prompt for one bug, function or stack trace.**
> Instead of dumping a whole repository (Repomix, gitingest) or whole files into ChatGPT, Claude or Cursor, `ast-pack` parses your repo with **Tree-sitter** into a cross-file call graph, starts at a symbol, `file:line` or raw stack trace, walks callers and callees N hops, pulls in every type definition and constant they use, and prunes everything else into a **syntactically valid** bundle with exact file/line headers.
> **Install:** `pip install ast-pack` · **Run:** `ast-pack processPayment` · **Measured:** 87–98.7% fewer tokens than the whole repo on Flask, httpx, Gin, chi, Hono, Zod and ripgrep ([benchmarks](benchmarks/RESULTS.md)).

Python · TypeScript · JavaScript/JSX · Go · Rust — CLI, `--json` for agents, MCP server, local HTTP/WebSocket API.

```bash
pip install ast-pack            # or, before the PyPI release: pipx install git+https://github.com/ginckl/ast-pack
ast-pack processPayment         # symbol → context bundle on stdout
ast-pack src/pay/service.py:42  # the function enclosing a line
pytest 2>&1 | ast-pack          # a stack trace from stdin
ast-pack Client.send -d 1 --copy  # copy to clipboard
ast-pack --ui                   # local web app + API
```

## What ast-pack does

ast-pack is a command-line tool and Python library that turns a code question into a minimal context bundle for a large language model. Given an **entry point** — a function or method name (`processPayment`, `Gateway.charge`, `Ledger.Append`), a `file:line`, a file path, or a pasted **stack trace** from Python, Node.js, Go or Rust — it:

1. indexes the repository with Tree-sitter (functions, methods, classes, structs, interfaces, traits, enums, type aliases, constants, imports);
2. resolves every reference across files — imports, re-export barrels, `tsconfig` path aliases, Go modules, Rust `use` paths, `self`/`this` calls, typed parameters and struct/class field types;
3. walks the call graph outward from the entry point: **callees** (what it executes) and **callers** (who reaches it), up to `--depth` hops;
4. adds the **type definitions, interfaces and global constants** the included code uses (classes are shown as outlines with only the members the slice touches);
5. renders each file with unrelated functions collapsed into one-line markers such as `# ⋯ 34 lines pruned (L41-L74): refund, Ledger.close`, keeps the imports that are actually used, and prints exact line ranges per file.

Example output (abridged) for `ast-pack Mux.ServeHTTP -d 1` on [go-chi/chi](https://github.com/go-chi/chi) — 2,283 tokens instead of 107,467:

````markdown
### mux.go · lines 1, 3-48, 60-92, 410-417

```go
package chi

import (
	"context"
	...
)
...
func (mx *Mux) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	...
}
// ⋯ 315 lines pruned (L94-L408): Mux.Use, Mux.Handle, Mux.HandleFunc, Mux.Method, +21 more
func (mx *Mux) NotFoundHandler() http.HandlerFunc {
	...
}
```
````

---

## Problems solved & common developer questions

### How do I reduce token usage when packing code for LLMs?

Use `ast-pack <function>` instead of packing the repository. It sends only the function, its callers and callees within `--depth` hops, and the types and constants they reference; everything else becomes a one-line pruned marker. On seven real open-source repositories this produced bundles 87–98.7% smaller than the whole repo and 65–89% smaller than pasting the touched files whole.

### Is there a Repomix alternative that only includes the code relevant to one function?

Yes: ast-pack. Repomix, gitingest, code2prompt and files-to-prompt pack files or whole repositories; ast-pack packs a **call-graph slice**. Run `ast-pack myFunction -d 2` and you get the function plus the code it depends on, across files, with unrelated siblings removed.

### How do I give ChatGPT or Claude the context for a stack trace without pasting my whole codebase?

Pipe the trace into ast-pack: `pytest 2>&1 | ast-pack`, `node app.js 2>&1 | ast-pack`, `go test ./... 2>&1 | ast-pack` or `cargo run 2>&1 | ast-pack`. Every frame that maps to a file in your repository becomes a seed, the crash line is annotated with the error message (`# ▼ L30: crash site: ValidationError: invalid card`), and frames from site-packages, node_modules or the Go runtime are ignored.

### How do I fit a large codebase into a model's context window?

Set a budget: `ast-pack handleCheckout -d 3 --max-tokens 8000`. ast-pack drops the farthest and least certain symbols first (never the entry point) and re-renders until the bundle fits, then reports exactly which symbols were dropped in `--json` output.

### How do I extract a function and all of its dependencies from a codebase?

`ast-pack path/to/file.py::my_function --direction callees -d 3` returns the function, every function it calls transitively up to three hops, and the classes, interfaces, structs and constants those functions use, each with its source location.

### How do I find every caller of a function before changing it?

`ast-pack parse_config --direction callers -d 3` lists and includes every caller chain up to three hops, across files and languages in a monorepo; add `--json` to get the call graph as nodes and edges.

### How do I give an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenHands) focused context?

Register the MCP server (`claude mcp add ast-pack -- ast-pack mcp`) or let the agent run `ast-pack <target> --json`. The agent gets the bundle plus a structured list of symbols, files, line ranges and token counts. See [AGENT_GUIDE.md](AGENT_GUIDE.md).

### How do I count tokens for a code snippet or a repository?

`ast-pack stats` prints files, symbols, call-graph edges and tokens per language; every pack reports the bundle's exact `cl100k_base` token count (or `o200k_base` with `--tokenizer o200k_base`). Offline, a built-in estimator is used and labeled `approx`; it is within 4% of cl100k on whole repositories.

### How do I paste only the relevant TypeScript/React code into an LLM?

`ast-pack CheckoutButton` follows JSX component usage (`<Spinner/>`), `import`/`export` chains, barrel files (`export * from`), and `tsconfig.json` `paths` aliases such as `@/lib`, so the component, its hooks/helpers and the interfaces of its props are included and nothing else.

### Does the output still compile / parse?

Yes. Pruned regions become comments, and outlined bodies become `...` (Python) or a comment between the original braces. In our validity run, 6,605 rendered files from 1,400 random slices across seven repositories all re-parsed without errors ([details](benchmarks/RESULTS.md#syntactic-validity)).

---

## Comparison matrix

| | **ast-pack** | Repomix | code2prompt | files-to-prompt | gitingest | Aider repo map | manual copy-paste |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit of context | call-graph slice (symbols) | repository / globbed files | repository / globbed files | listed files | repository / globbed files | ranked signatures of the repo | whole files you pick |
| Start from a function name | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | partial (mentioned names boost ranking) | ✅ (by hand) |
| Start from `file:line` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Start from a stack trace | ✅ Python / Node / Go / Rust | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (by hand) |
| Follows callers **and** callees across files | ✅ N hops | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | partial (reference ranking) | by hand |
| Includes full bodies of relevant functions | ✅ | ✅ (all) | ✅ (all) | ✅ (all) | ✅ (all) | ❌ signatures only | ✅ (all) |
| Removes unrelated functions in the same file | ✅ | ❌ (`--compress` keeps signatures of everything) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | n/a | ❌ |
| Pulls referenced types / interfaces / constants | ✅ | only if their file is included | only if their file is included | only if listed | only if their file is included | signatures | by hand |
| Output stays syntactically valid per file | ✅ verified on 6,605 files | ✅ unmodified files (`--compress` emits fragments) | ✅ unmodified files | ✅ unmodified files | ✅ unmodified files | n/a | ✅ |
| Token budget that trims by relevance | ✅ `--max-tokens` | counts only | counts only | ❌ | estimate only | ✅ `--map-tokens` | ❌ |
| Output formats | Markdown, XML, plain, `--json` with [schema](schema.json) | XML, Markdown, plain | Handlebars templates | plain, Claude XML (`--cxml`) | text digest | text map inside aider | — |
| Agent integration | `--json` on every command, MCP server | MCP server | CLI | CLI | CLI / web | inside aider | — |
| Install | `pip install ast-pack` | `npx repomix` | `cargo install code2prompt` | `pip install files-to-prompt` | `pip install gitingest` | part of `aider` | — |
| Bundle for one function in a 100k–1M-token repo | **2k–25k tokens measured** | ≈ whole repo unless you hand-pick files | ≈ whole repo unless filtered | the files you list | ≈ whole repo unless filtered | the configured map size (signatures, no bodies) | whole files |

The other tools are excellent for "give the model my whole small repo" or a repository overview; ast-pack is for "give the model exactly what it needs to reason about *this* code path". Feature rows reflect each project's documented behaviour at the time of writing; corrections are welcome via pull request.

---

## Benchmarks

Default options (`-d 1` / `-d 2`, callers + callees, tests excluded), exact `cl100k_base` tokens, pinned commits. Full table, method and reproduction script: [benchmarks/RESULTS.md](benchmarks/RESULTS.md).

| repository | language | entry point | depth | bundle tokens | repo tokens | saved vs repo | saved vs touched files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pallets/flask | Python | `Flask.full_dispatch_request` | 1 | 10,834 | 134,903 | **92.0%** | 70.9% |
| encode/httpx | Python | `Client.send` | 1 | 7,567 | 133,516 | **94.3%** | 80.2% |
| gin-gonic/gin | Go | `Context.JSON` | 2 | 5,592 | 196,695 | **97.2%** | 83.6% |
| go-chi/chi | Go | `Mux.ServeHTTP` | 1 | 2,283 | 107,467 | **97.9%** | 82.8% |
| honojs/hono | TypeScript | `Hono.fetch` | 1 | 22,127 | 752,557 | **97.1%** | 69.1% |
| colinhacks/zod | TypeScript | `ZodString._parse` | 2 | 15,484 | 1,003,297 | **98.5%** | 68.0% |
| BurntSushi/ripgrep | Rust | `search_path` | 2 | 21,606 | 460,732 | **95.3%** | 88.1% |

Indexing a 1M-token TypeScript repo (zod, 522 files) takes about 1.1 s cold with ~77 MB peak memory; a pack takes 10–150 ms. Re-runs use an mtime-keyed parse cache.

---

## Installation

```bash
pip install ast-pack
```

Before the first PyPI release, install from GitHub:

```bash
pipx install git+https://github.com/ginckl/ast-pack
```

Requirements: Python 3.10+. Tree-sitter grammars for Python, TypeScript/TSX, JavaScript, Go and Rust are installed as wheels — no compiler, no Node.js, no language servers. `tiktoken` provides exact token counts; it downloads its vocabulary once and ast-pack falls back to an estimator when offline.

---

## Usage

### Pack a function, method or type

```bash
ast-pack processPayment                       # bare name
ast-pack Gateway.charge                       # Class.method / Type.method
ast-pack ledger.Append                        # Go package.Func or Type.Method
ast-pack src/payments/service.py::process     # disambiguate by file
ast-pack processPayment refundPayment         # several seeds in one bundle
```

### Pack from a line or a file

```bash
ast-pack src/billing/invoice.rs:33            # innermost symbol enclosing line 33
ast-pack web/src/lib/api.ts                   # every top-level symbol of the file
```

### Pack from a stack trace

```bash
pytest -x 2>&1 | ast-pack -d 1
ast-pack trace crash.log
pbpaste | ast-pack --copy
```

Supported formats: Python tracebacks, Node.js/V8 (`at fn (file:line:col)`, including `file://` and `webpack-internal://` paths), Go panics/goroutine dumps, Rust `panicked at` messages and `RUST_BACKTRACE` frames. Absolute paths from CI or another machine are matched to repository files by longest path suffix.

### Control the slice

```bash
ast-pack handler -d 3                         # more hops
ast-pack handler --direction callees          # only what it calls
ast-pack handler --direction callers          # only who calls it
ast-pack handler --max-tokens 6000            # fit a budget
ast-pack handler --min-confidence 1.0         # only exactly-resolved calls
ast-pack handler --include-tests              # also follow test files
ast-pack handler --type-depth 0 --no-types    # behaviour only, no type definitions
```

### Shape the output

```bash
ast-pack handler -f xml                       # <file path=... lines=...> blocks (good for Claude)
ast-pack handler -f plain                     # ==> path <== headers
ast-pack handler --line-numbers               # prefix kept lines with original numbers
ast-pack handler --strip-comments             # drop comment-only lines
ast-pack handler -p "Why does this double-charge?"   # put the task before the context
ast-pack handler -o context.md --copy         # write a file and copy to clipboard
```

---

## CLI reference

```text
ast-pack [pack] TARGET... [options]     build a bundle (default command)
ast-pack trace [FILE|-] [options]       pack a stack trace from a file or stdin
ast-pack search QUERY [-n N] [--kind K] fuzzy symbol search
ast-pack stats                          files / symbols / edges / tokens per language
ast-pack serve [--host H] [--port P] [--open] [--watch-interval S]
ast-pack --ui                           same as `serve --open`
ast-pack mcp                            Model Context Protocol server on stdio
```

| option | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-C, --repo DIR` | `.` | repository root |
| `-d, --depth N` | `2` | call-graph hops |
| `--direction` | `both` | `both`, `callers`, `callees` |
| `-b, --max-tokens N` | none | token budget |
| `--max-fanout N` | `30` | max callers/callees followed per symbol (closest first) |
| `--type-depth N` | `2` | levels of type/constant definitions |
| `--no-types` | off | skip type/constant closure |
| `--min-confidence X` | `0.5` | drop call edges resolved below this confidence |
| `--include-tests` | off | follow test files (auto-on when the target is a test) |
| `-f, --format` | `markdown` | `markdown`, `xml`, `plain` |
| `--line-numbers`, `--strip-comments`, `--no-imports`, `--no-map` | off | output shaping |
| `-p, --prompt TEXT` | none | task text before the context |
| `-o, --output FILE`, `--copy` | stdout | destination |
| `--json` | off | one JSON document on stdout ([schema.json](schema.json)) |
| `--no-bundle` | off | with `--json`: omit code, keep graph + stats |
| `--depth-profile` | off | bundle size at every depth 0..6 |
| `--include GLOB`, `--exclude GLOB`, `--lang LANGS` | all | limit what is indexed |
| `--tokenizer NAME` | `cl100k_base` | `cl100k_base`, `o200k_base`, `approx` |
| `--no-cache` | off | skip the on-disk parse cache |

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` error, `2` nothing matched (JSON error includes `suggestions`).

---

## JSON output for agents and scripts

Every command accepts `--json` and prints exactly one JSON document described by [schema.json](schema.json):

```bash
cd chi && ast-pack Mux.ServeHTTP -d 1 --json | jq '.stats'
```

```json
{
  "symbols": 11, "files": 4, "bundle_tokens": 2283, "repo_tokens": 107467,
  "touched_file_tokens": 13258, "saved_pct": 97.88, "saved_vs_files_pct": 82.78,
  "tokenizer": "cl100k_base", "tokenizer_exact": true, "elapsed_ms": 17.76, "index_generation": 1
}
```

On very small repositories the slice map and headers can cost more than they save versus whole files; `--no-map` removes the map.

A pack result contains `seeds`, `nodes` (symbol, kind, path, line range, hop, role `seed|callee|caller|type|value|container`, mode `full|outline|header`, confidence), `edges` (`call|type|value`), `files` (line ranges and `code`/`pruned` segments), `bundle`, `dropped`, `warnings`, `suggestions`, and `trace` (language, error message, crash site, frames).

---

## MCP server (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf)

```bash
claude mcp add ast-pack -- ast-pack mcp -C /path/to/repo
```

Generic MCP client configuration:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "ast-pack": { "command": "ast-pack", "args": ["mcp", "-C", "/path/to/repo"] } } }
```

Tools: `pack_context(target, depth?, direction?, max_tokens?, format?, repo?)`, `search_symbols(query, limit?, repo?)`, `repo_stats(repo?)`. The index is kept in memory and refreshed incrementally on every call.

---

## HTTP / WebSocket API and web UI

`ast-pack serve` (or `ast-pack --ui`) starts a local server on `127.0.0.1:7878` that watches the repository and re-indexes changed files:

| endpoint | purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | version, root, index generation |
| `GET /api/stats` | index statistics |
| `GET /api/search?q=` | fuzzy symbol search |
| `POST /api/pack` | body: pack options (`targets`, `depth`, `direction`, `max_tokens`, `format`, `depth_profile`, ...) |
| `GET /api/file?path=` | full source of an indexed file (to expand pruned segments) |
| `GET /api/graph?limit=` | repository overview graph |
| `WS /ws` | `pack` / `search` / `file` messages (latest-wins while typing) and `index_updated` pushes |

The interactive web UI (command bar, animated force-directed graph, hop-depth slider, token-savings counter, code preview with expandable pruned segments) is being built on top of this API in `ui/`. Until its bundle ships in the package, `/` serves an API index page.

---

## Python library API

```python
from ast_pack import RepoIndex, PackOptions, pack

index = RepoIndex.build("path/to/repo")
result = pack(index, PackOptions(targets=["processPayment"], depth=2, max_tokens=8000))
print(result.bundle)
print(result.bundle_tokens, result.saved_pct)
for node in result.to_dict()["nodes"]:
    print(node["role"], node["qualname"], node["path"], node["start_line"])
index.refresh()  # re-parse only changed files
```

---

## How it works

```text
scanner ──► extractors (Tree-sitter, per language) ──► RepoIndex ──► slicer ──► renderer ──► bundle
  git ls-files        symbols · refs · imports            name resolution     BFS callers/   line plan:
  .gitignore          field types · local types           call/type/value     callees +      full / outline /
  size & vendor       comment lines                       edges + reverse     type closure   header + pruned
  filters             (parallel, cached by mtime)         index               + budget       markers
```

- **Extraction** (`src/ast_pack/extractors/`): one Tree-sitter walker per language records symbols with exact ranges (doc comments, decorators and attributes included), outline anchors (where bodies start), imports, and every referenced name with its receiver (`self.repo.save` → `save` on `self.repo`). Parameters, locals and loop variables are filtered; typed parameters and struct/class fields record their types.
- **Resolution** (`src/ast_pack/index.py`): bare names resolve through the file, its imports (following re-export chains), and language scope (Go package directories, Rust crates). Member calls resolve through `self`/`this`/receivers, declared field types, typed locals, module aliases and base classes/traits. Calls on values of unknown type are matched by name only when at most three methods share it and the name is not ubiquitous (`get`, `close`, …), with confidence < 1.
- **Slicing** (`src/ast_pack/slicer.py`): two breadth-first walks (callees and callers) that never mix, a per-node fan-out cap that prefers nearby code, then a closure over type and value edges.
- **Rendering** (`src/ast_pack/render.py`): a per-file line plan; Python classes that lose every statement get `...`; markers that would cost more tokens than the code they hide are replaced by the code.

---

## Limitations

- Resolution is static and name-based, not a type checker: dynamic dispatch, monkey-patching, reflection, dependency injection containers and calls through untyped values can be missed or (with confidence < 1) over-included. Use `--min-confidence 1.0` for exact edges only.
- Callers reached only through interfaces/traits (Go interface satisfaction, Rust `dyn Trait`) are not linked to their implementations.
- Macros (Rust) and decorators that generate code are treated as references, not expanded.
- Supported languages: Python, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript/JSX, Go, Rust. Other files are ignored.
- `tree-sitter` 0.26.0's Python binding crashes on some real-world files, so the dependency is pinned below 0.26 until that is fixed upstream.

# ast-pack — guide for AI coding agents

This file is written for autonomous coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenHands, Aider, Codex-style agents, custom tool-calling agents). It tells you when to use ast-pack, how to install it, and how to parse its output deterministically.

## When to use ast-pack

Use ast-pack when you need to understand or change a specific code path and would otherwise read many whole files. Typical triggers:

- Your user reports a bug in a named function (`processPayment double-charges`). → `ast-pack processPayment --json`
- You have a stack trace or failing test output. → pipe it: `pytest -x 2>&1 | ast-pack --json`
- You are about to modify a function and need every caller. → `ast-pack fn --direction callers -d 3 --json`
- You need a function plus everything it depends on (helpers, types, constants). → `ast-pack fn --direction callees -d 3 --json`
- Your context window is tight. → add `--max-tokens 8000`
- Your user asks for "the relevant code" to paste into another LLM. → `ast-pack fn -d 2 --copy` or `-o context.md`

Do not use ast-pack for whole-repository overviews, for files in unsupported languages, or when you already have the exact code in context.

Supported languages: Python, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript/JSX, Go, Rust.

## Install (run automatically)

```bash
python -m pip install ast-pack
```

If the package is not yet on PyPI or pip is restricted:

```bash
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/ginckl/ast-pack"
```

Verify with `ast-pack --version`. No compiler, Node.js or language server is needed. Exact token counts need `tiktoken`'s vocabulary (downloaded once); offline, counts are estimates and `stats.tokenizer` is `"approx"`.

## The one command you need

```bash
ast-pack <TARGET> -C <REPO_ROOT> -d 2 --json
```

`TARGET` may be:

| form | example |
|---|---|
| symbol | `processPayment`, `Gateway.charge`, `Ledger.Append`, `ledger.Append` |
| file-qualified symbol | `src/pay/service.py::process_payment` (use this to disambiguate) |
| line | `src/billing/invoice.rs:33` |
| file | `web/src/lib/api.ts` (all top-level symbols) |
| stack trace | the raw text as one argument, or `-` / piped stdin, or `ast-pack trace FILE` |

Several targets in one call are merged into one bundle.

## Parsing the JSON

stdout is exactly one JSON document (schema: `schema.json`). Check `ok` first, then use:

| field | use |
|---|---|
| `bundle` | the prompt-ready context (Markdown by default; `-f xml` for `<file path=… lines=…>` blocks) |
| `seeds` | symbol ids the target resolved to |
| `nodes[]` | every included symbol: `id`, `qualname`, `kind`, `path`, `start_line`, `end_line`, `hop`, `role` (`seed`/`callee`/`caller`/`type`/`value`/`container`), `mode` (`full`/`outline`/`header`), `confidence` |
| `edges[]` | `source`, `target`, `kind` (`call`/`type`/`value`), `confidence`, `line` |
| `files[]` | `path`, `ranges` (kept line ranges), `segments` (`code` / `pruned` with hidden symbol names) |
| `stats` | `bundle_tokens`, `repo_tokens`, `saved_pct`, `tokenizer`, `elapsed_ms` |
| `trace` | for stack traces: `language`, `error`, `crash_site` (`repo_path`, `line`, `symbol`), `frames[]` |
| `warnings`, `suggestions` | ambiguity notes and "did you mean" names |
| `dropped` | symbol ids removed to satisfy `--max-tokens` |

Use `--no-bundle` when you only need the graph (who calls what, which files and line ranges) and will read code yourself.

### Exit codes

- `0` success
- `2` nothing matched → read `error.suggestions` and retry with one of them, or qualify the name as `path::name`
- `1` other error (bad repo path, unreadable file)

### Recipes

```bash
# Callers of a function, as "path:line qualname"
ast-pack parse_config --direction callers -d 3 --json --no-bundle \
  | jq -r '.nodes[] | select(.role=="caller") | "\(.path):\(.start_line) \(.qualname)"'

# Where did it crash?
pytest -x 2>&1 | ast-pack --json --no-bundle | jq '.trace.crash_site'

# Files and line ranges to open
ast-pack Client.send -d 1 --json --no-bundle | jq -r '.files[] | "\(.path) \(.ranges)"'

# Find the right symbol name first
ast-pack search charge --json | jq -r '.results[] | "\(.qualname) \(.path):\(.start_line)"'
```

## Interpreting the bundle

- Each file section is headed `### path · lines a-b, c-d` (Markdown) or `<file path="…" lines="…">` (XML). Line numbers are the original file's.
- `# ⋯ 34 lines pruned (L41-L74): refund, Ledger.close` (or `// ⋯ …`) marks code that was removed because it is unrelated to the target. If you need it, read those lines from disk.
- `...  # ⋯ 3 lines` (Python) or `// ⋯ 3 lines` inside braces marks a method body omitted because the class is only used as a type; the signature is accurate.
- `# ▼ L30: crash site: …` / `// ▼ L30: …` annotates lines from the stack trace or the `file:line` target.
- The slice map lists every symbol with its role and why it was included (`← caller of`, `→ called by`).
- Edges with `confidence < 1` were resolved by method name on a value of unknown type; verify them before relying on them. `--min-confidence 1.0` keeps only exact resolutions.

## MCP integration

```bash
claude mcp add ast-pack -- ast-pack mcp -C /path/to/repo
```

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "ast-pack": { "command": "ast-pack", "args": ["mcp", "-C", "/path/to/repo"] } } }
```

Tools: `pack_context` (`target`, `depth`, `direction`, `max_tokens`, `format`, `repo`), `search_symbols` (`query`, `limit`, `repo`), `repo_stats` (`repo`). `pack_context` returns the bundle as text plus `structuredContent` with `stats`, `seeds`, `symbols`, `warnings`, `trace`.

## Local API

`ast-pack serve -C REPO --json` prints `{"url": …, "ws": …}` and serves `POST /api/pack` (same options as the CLI, JSON body), `GET /api/search?q=`, `GET /api/file?path=`, `GET /api/stats`, and a WebSocket at `/ws`. It re-indexes changed files automatically.

## Limits to keep in mind

Resolution is static: dynamic dispatch, reflection, monkey-patching and DI containers can hide edges; Go interface and Rust `dyn Trait` call sites are not linked to implementations. Test files are excluded from the walk unless the target is a test or `--include-tests` is set.

---

# JSON output contract (schema.json)

Every ast-pack command run with --json prints exactly one JSON document matching one of these shapes. Discriminate on `command` and `ok`. Exit code 0 = success, 1 = error, 2 = nothing matched / bad usage.

### `envelope`

- `schema_version` (const '1.0')
- `tool` (const 'ast-pack')
- `version` (string)
- `command` (enum: pack, trace, search, stats, serve, None)
- `ok` (boolean)

### `errorResult`

- `ok` (const False)
- `error` (object)

### `symbol`

- `id` (string): stable id: <path>::<qualname> (with @L<line> if duplicated)
- `name` (string)
- `qualname` (string): e.g. Gateway.charge, Ledger.Append
- `kind` (enum: function, method, macro, class, struct, interface, trait, enum, type, union, const, variable, static, module, impl, block)
- `language` (enum: python, typescript, tsx, javascript, rust, go)
- `path` (string): repository-relative POSIX path
- `start_line` (integer): 1-based, includes leading doc comments / decorators
- `end_line` (integer)
- `signature` (string)
- `tokens` (integer): tokens of the full symbol source
- `score` (number): search only

### `node`

- `hop` (integer): call-graph distance from the nearest seed
- `role` (enum: seed, callee, caller, type, value, container)
- `mode` (enum: full, outline, header): full source, signatures only, or container header
- `via` (['string', 'null']): id of the node that pulled this one in
- `via_kind` (enum: calls, called_by, uses_type, uses_value, contains, None)
- `confidence` (number)
- `truncated_neighbors` (integer): callers/callees skipped by --max-fanout

### `edge`

- `source` (string)
- `target` (string)
- `kind` (enum: call, type, value)
- `confidence` (number): 1.0 = resolved through definitions/imports/types; <1 = name match on an untyped receiver
- `line` (integer)

### `segment`

- `kind` (enum: code, pruned)
- `start` (integer)
- `end` (integer)
- `text` (string): rendered code, or the one-line pruned marker
- `symbols` (array): pruned: names of the definitions hidden
- `tokens` (integer): code: rendered tokens; pruned: tokens hidden

### `file`

- `path` (string)
- `language` (string)
- `ranges` (array)
- `symbols` (array)
- `file_tokens` (integer)
- `file_lines` (integer)
- `kept_tokens` (integer)
- `segments` (array of segment): omitted with --no-bundle
- `text` (string): omitted with --no-bundle

### `frame`

- `path` (string): path as printed in the trace
- `line` (integer)
- `function` (['string', 'null'])
- `repo_path` (['string', 'null']): matching repository file, null if outside the repo
- `symbol` (['string', 'null'])

### `packResult`

- `command` (const 'pack')
- `query` (object)
- `seeds` (array)
- `stats` (object)
- `nodes` (array of node)
- `edges` (array of edge)
- `files` (array of file)
- `bundle` (string): the prompt-ready context; omitted with --no-bundle
- `dropped` (array): symbol ids removed to meet --max-tokens
- `warnings` (array)
- `suggestions` (array)
- `trace` (['object', 'null'])
- `depth_profile` (array)
- `output_file` (['string', 'null'])
- `copied_to_clipboard` (['boolean', 'null'])

### `searchResult`

- `command` (const 'search')
- `query` (string)
- `results` (array of symbol)

### `statsResult`

- `command` (const 'stats')
- `root` (string)
- `files` (integer)
- `symbols` (integer)
- `edges` (integer)
- `tokens` (integer)
- `lines` (integer)
- `tokenizer` (string)
- `languages` (object)
- `symbol_kinds` (object)
- `edge_kinds` (object)
- `parse_errors` (integer)
- `timing` (object)

### `serveResult`

- `command` (const 'serve')
- `url` (string)
- `ws` (string)
- `root` (string)
- `ui` (boolean)

---

# Internals

## Command-line interface (`src/ast_pack/cli.py`)

Command-line interface.

    ast-pack processPayment                 # pack a symbol (pack is the default command)
    ast-pack src/pay/service.py:42 -d 3     # pack the symbol enclosing a line
    pytest 2>&1 | ast-pack                  # pack a stack trace from stdin
    ast-pack search pay --json              # fuzzy symbol search
    ast-pack stats --json                   # repository index statistics
    ast-pack --ui                           # local web UI + API (same as `ast-pack serve --open`)
    ast-pack mcp                            # Model Context Protocol server over stdio

Every command accepts ``--json`` and then prints exactly one JSON document on
stdout (schema: ``schema.json``). Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 nothing
matched / bad usage.

## Engine (`src/ast_pack/engine.py`)

High-level API: ``pack(index, PackOptions) -> PackResult``.

This is the one function the CLI, the HTTP/WebSocket server and library users
all call. It resolves targets to seed symbols, builds the slice, enforces an
optional token budget, renders the bundle and reports exact token savings.

## Entry-point resolution (`src/ast_pack/entry.py`)

Entry-point resolution: symbol names, ``file:line`` targets and stack traces.

A *target* string is classified automatically:

1. **Stack trace** – multi-line text containing Python, Node.js/V8, Go
   (panic / goroutine dumps) or Rust (panic + backtrace) frames. Every frame
   that maps to a file in the repository becomes a seed; the innermost
   in-repo frame is marked as the crash site.
2. **file:line[:col]** – the innermost symbol enclosing that line.
3. **file path** – every top-level symbol in the file.
4. **symbol** – ``name``, ``Class.method``, ``Type::method``, ``pkg.Func`` or
   ``path/to/file.py::name``; exact matches win, then case-insensitive ones.

## Repository index and resolver (`src/ast_pack/index.py`)

Repository index: parsed files, symbol table and the cross-file graph.

``RepoIndex.build(root)`` scans the repository, extracts every supported file
with Tree-sitter (in parallel for large repos, reusing an on-disk cache keyed
by mtime/size), then resolves every reference to concrete symbols:

* bare names resolve through the file's own definitions, its imports
  (following re-export chains and barrel files), then language scope rules
  (Go: same package directory, Rust: same crate);
* ``self.x`` / ``this.x`` / ``Self::x`` / Go receivers resolve to methods of
  the owning type, then its base classes / implemented traits;
* ``module.x`` / ``pkg.X`` / ``ns.x`` resolve through module bindings to the
  target file(s);
* calls on values of unknown type (``obj.save()``) resolve only when at most
  three methods in the repo share that name, with reduced confidence.

The result is a directed graph of ``call`` / ``type`` / ``value`` edges with
a reverse index for caller lookups.

## Graph walk (`src/ast_pack/slicer.py`)

Graph walk: from seed symbols to the set of symbols that belong in a slice.

Two breadth-first walks start at the seeds:

* **callees** – follows outgoing ``call`` edges (what the seed executes),
* **callers** – follows incoming ``call`` edges (who reaches the seed).

They never mix (a caller's other callees are siblings, not context), and each
node's fan-out is capped so a utility called from 500 places cannot flood the
slice; the closest callers (same file, then same directory) win.

Then a **closure** pass pulls in everything the included code needs to be
understood but that is not "behaviour": type definitions (classes, structs,
interfaces, traits, enums, aliases) and constants/globals, recursively up to
``type_depth`` levels. Python/TypeScript classes reached only as types are
rendered as outlines (fields + method signatures); methods pull in the header
of their enclosing class/impl so the code stays syntactically valid.

## Rendering (`src/ast_pack/render.py`)

Rendering: turn a slice into per-file code views and the final bundle.

For each file the renderer builds a line plan:

* ``full`` symbols keep every line (including leading doc comments and
  decorators/attributes);
* ``outline`` symbols keep signatures; bodies become ``...`` (Python) or a
  ``// … N lines`` stub between the braces; docstrings and fields stay;
* ``header`` containers keep the class/impl/trait opening lines, fields and
  the closing brace so kept members stay syntactically valid;
* imports are kept only when they bind a name the kept code uses.

Everything else collapses into *pruned* segments rendered as a single
comment line such as ``# ⋯ 34 lines pruned (L41-L74): refund, Ledger.close``.
Because markers are comments and stubs are valid bodies, the output of each
file parses in its own language.

## Token counting (`src/ast_pack/tokens.py`)

Token counting.

ast-pack reports token savings, so counting must be fast and deterministic.
When ``tiktoken`` is installed and its BPE file is available (it is downloaded
once and cached by tiktoken), counts are exact for the chosen encoding
(``cl100k_base`` by default, ``o200k_base`` also supported). Otherwise a
calibrated estimator is used and every report says ``tokenizer: "approx"``.

The estimator splits text the way BPE pre-tokenizers do (letter runs, digit
groups, punctuation runs, whitespace runs) and charges each piece by length.
Its weights were fitted against cl100k_base on Python, TypeScript, Go and Rust
sources; on whole files it lands within a few percent of the real count.

## File discovery (`src/ast_pack/scanner.py`)

Repository file discovery.

Inside a git work tree the file list comes from ``git ls-files`` (tracked plus
untracked-but-not-ignored files), which honours every ``.gitignore`` exactly.
Outside git, the tree is walked and the root ``.gitignore`` is applied with
``pathspec``. Vendored, generated and dependency directories are always
skipped, as are minified bundles and very large files.

## Extractors (`src/ast_pack/extractors/base.py`)

Shared machinery for the per-language Tree-sitter extractors.

An extractor turns one source file into:

* ``Symbol`` records (functions, methods, classes, structs, interfaces,
  traits, enums, type aliases, constants, module-level variables) with exact
  line ranges, outline anchors (where bodies start/end) and the names each
  symbol references;
* ``ImportBinding`` records describing which local names come from which
  module, used later for cross-file resolution;
* the set of comment-only lines (for ``--strip-comments``).

Reference collection is a top-down walk. Each language implements
``visit(node, out)`` which either records references for ``node`` and
returns the children to descend into, or returns ``None`` to descend into all
named children. Local bindings (parameters, assignment targets, loop
variables...) are collected separately and filtered out of bare references.

## HTTP and WebSocket server (`src/ast_pack/server.py`)

Local HTTP + WebSocket API (and static host for the web UI).

REST (all JSON):

    GET  /api/health                 version, repo root, index generation
    GET  /api/stats                  RepoIndex.stats()
    GET  /api/search?q=&limit=&kind= fuzzy symbol search
    POST /api/pack                   body: PackOptions fields -> PackResult.to_dict()
    GET  /api/file?path=             full file text (to expand pruned segments)
    GET  /api/graph?limit=           repository overview graph (highest-degree symbols)
    POST /api/refresh                force a re-scan

WebSocket ``/ws`` (JSON messages, ``id`` echoes back):

    -> {"type": "pack",   "id": 7, "params": {...PackOptions}}
    <- {"type": "pack_result", "id": 7, "result": {...}}
    -> {"type": "search", "id": 8, "q": "proc", "limit": 12}
    <- {"type": "search_result", "id": 8, "results": [...]}
    -> {"type": "file", "id": 9, "path": "src/x.py"}
    <- {"type": "file_result", "id": 9, "file": {...}}
    <- {"type": "index_updated", "stats": {...}}      (pushed when files change)
    <- {"type": "error", "id": 7, "message": "..."}

``pack`` and ``search`` are latest-wins per connection: while one request is
computing, newer ones replace older queued ones, so typing in the command
bar never builds a backlog.

The server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and only ever serves files that are
part of the index.

## MCP server (`src/ast_pack/mcp.py`)

Model Context Protocol server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, newline-delimited).

Register it with an MCP client, e.g. Claude Code::

    claude mcp add ast-pack -- ast-pack mcp -C /path/to/repo

Tools:

* ``pack_context`` – build a context bundle for a symbol, ``file:line`` or a
  pasted stack trace (returns the bundle as text plus structured stats);
* ``search_symbols`` – fuzzy symbol search;
* ``repo_stats`` – index statistics.

Each tool takes an optional ``repo`` argument; indexes are cached per root and
refreshed incrementally (only changed files are re-parsed) on every call.

---

# ast-pack benchmark results

Measured on 2026-11-04 with ast-pack 0.1.0, Python 3.13, 4 vCPU Linux container.
Reproduce with:

```bash
python benchmarks/bench.py --workdir /tmp/ast-pack-bench
```

Every repository is checked out at the pinned commit shown. Each row packs one
real entry point (`ast-pack <entry> -d <depth>` with default options: callers +
callees, type depth 2, test files excluded).

* **saved vs repo** – bundle tokens compared to the whole indexed repository
  (what whole-repo packers such as Repomix or gitingest emit by default).
* **saved vs whole files** – bundle tokens compared to pasting, in full, every
  file the slice touches (the "copy the relevant files" workaround).
* Bundle tokens include ast-pack's own headers and slice map.

## Token savings

Tokenizer: `cl100k_base`

| repo | language | entry point | depth | symbols | files | bundle tokens | repo tokens | saved vs repo | saved vs whole files | index / pack time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flask @ `49943b5` | Python | `Flask.full_dispatch_request` | 1 | 29 | 9 | 10,834 | 134,903 | **92.0%** | 70.9% | 0.24 s / 41 ms |
| flask @ `49943b5` | Python | `Flask.full_dispatch_request` | 2 | 50 | 11 | 16,280 | 134,903 | **87.9%** | 64.8% | 0.24 s / 59 ms |
| httpx @ `b5addb6` | Python | `Client.send` | 1 | 38 | 8 | 7,567 | 133,516 | **94.3%** | 80.2% | 0.54 s / 39 ms |
| httpx @ `b5addb6` | Python | `Client.send` | 2 | 82 | 13 | 17,176 | 133,516 | **87.1%** | 65.1% | 0.54 s / 67 ms |
| gin @ `0f09c3a` | Go | `Context.JSON` | 1 | 33 | 10 | 4,782 | 196,695 | **97.6%** | 86.0% | 0.35 s / 27 ms |
| gin @ `0f09c3a` | Go | `Context.JSON` | 2 | 41 | 10 | 5,592 | 196,695 | **97.2%** | 83.6% | 0.35 s / 27 ms |
| chi @ `9f8adb1` | Go | `Mux.ServeHTTP` | 1 | 11 | 4 | 2,283 | 107,467 | **97.9%** | 82.8% | 0.22 s / 12 ms |
| chi @ `9f8adb1` | Go | `Mux.ServeHTTP` | 2 | 11 | 4 | 2,283 | 107,467 | **97.9%** | 82.8% | 0.22 s / 11 ms |
| hono @ `8b7f9e9` | TypeScript | `Hono.fetch` | 1 | 125 | 27 | 22,127 | 752,557 | **97.1%** | 69.1% | 0.98 s / 135 ms |
| hono @ `8b7f9e9` | TypeScript | `Hono.fetch` | 2 | 142 | 30 | 25,248 | 752,557 | **96.7%** | 65.3% | 0.98 s / 114 ms |
| zod @ `77e72ec` | TypeScript | `ZodString._parse` | 1 | 61 | 5 | 13,086 | 1,003,297 | **98.7%** | 72.3% | 1.42 s / 71 ms |

| ripgrep @ `91f5d22` | Rust | `search_path` | 2 | 56 | 15 | 21,606 | 460,732 | **95.3%** | 88.1% | 0.72 s / 118 ms |

## Syntactic validity

`benchmarks/validity.py` packs 200 random functions / methods / classes /
structs per repository at depth 1 and re-parses every rendered file (Python
with `ast.parse`, the other languages with Tree-sitter error nodes).

| repository | rendered files checked | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| flask | 1040 | 0 |
| httpx | 1008 | 0 |
| gin | 1061 | 0 |
| chi | 686 | 0 |
| hono | 1105 | 0 |
| zod | 1054 | 0 |
| ripgrep | 651 | 0 |

## Indexing cost

| repository | files | symbols | edges | tokens | cold index | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flask | 83 | 1,068 | 2,505 | 134,903 | 0.25 s | 64 MB |
| httpx | 60 | 1,253 | 3,449 | 133,516 | 0.75 s | 64 MB |
| gin | 99 | 1,722 | 4,641 | 196,695 | 0.36 s | 66 MB |
| chi | 89 | 557 | 1,362 | 107,467 | 0.24 s | 63 MB |
| hono | 453 | 2,102 | 5,120 | 752,557 | 0.90 s | 68 MB |
| zod | 522 | 5,113 | 19,143 | 1,003,297 | 1.11 s | 77 MB |
| ripgrep | 102 | 3,846 | 9,802 | 460,732 | 0.71 s | 72 MB |

Warm runs reuse the on-disk parse cache (`~/.cache/ast-pack`) and only re-parse
files whose mtime or size changed.

## Token estimator accuracy

When tiktoken's vocabulary cannot be loaded (offline machines), ast-pack falls
back to a built-in estimator and labels output `tokenizer: "approx"`. Against
exact `cl100k_base` on 120 random files per repository:

| repository | exact | estimated | ratio | per-file p10–p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flask | 134,903 | 136,551 | 1.012 | 0.99–1.05 |
| httpx | 133,516 | 133,411 | 0.999 | 0.96–1.03 |
| gin | 196,695 | 189,194 | 0.962 | 0.92–1.01 |
| hono | 141,237 | 141,880 | 1.005 | 0.94–1.05 |
| zod | 175,592 | 176,899 | 1.007 | 0.91–1.09 |
| ripgrep | 460,732 | 461,311 | 1.001 | 0.97–1.04 |
